topics.label: Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture by linking to practical sessions and outlining the learning objectives on cancer genetics and instability.

topics.label: Tumor Virology and Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the discovery of proto-oncogenes via transforming viruses and the experimental assays used to test cell transformation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer mutation categories and illustrate how oncogenic and tumor-suppressive alterations disrupt cell cycle control and cellular function.

topics.label: Genetic Instability and Multi-Step Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how specific defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitosis generate genetic instability to accelerate multi-step tumor progression.

topics.label: Hereditary Cancer Predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how inherited gene mutations accelerate cancer onset in hereditary syndromes and evaluate whether genetic instability is required for tumor maintenance.

topics.label: Conclusion and Further Reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by reviewing the learning outcomes, recommending background reading, and previewing the next lecture.
